newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends lower after hitting historic low.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends lower after hitting historic low.

text.p: The won closed Monday's hectic trading sharply lower against the dollar after it plunged to an all-time low of 830.00 despite a series of interventions by the central bank, dealers said.
They said the Bank of Korea (BOK) sold dollars three times, at 823.40 and 826.60 in the morning session and 829.30 during afternoon trading.
The central bank denied it had intervened, but dealers said there were no other reasons for the dollar's brief fall.
Despite the rumoured intervention, the won closed lower at 828.80 after opening at 824.20.
The won fluctated in a 823.60-830.00 range.
"The greenback soared on some importer deals amid a shortage of dollars in the market," said a local bank dealer. "The intervention injected more dollar supply into the market."
Dealers forecast a weaker won tomorrow as many dealers are expected to continue covering short dollar positions.
"After dealers test the BOK's intention, they will place bid and offers tomorrow," said a foreign bank dealer.
Reflecting Monda's volatility, dealers said Tuesday's mid-rate was estimated be pegged at around 827.00 and 827.50 against 822.80 today. -- YEOM YOON-JEONG (822) 727 5647
